title: Reforming CCA Access in Our Schools
what_it_is: Reforming CCA Access in Our Schools

sections.label: Primary school CCA trial removal
sections.summary: The Ministry piloted removing CCA selection trials in eight primary schools in 2020, and about two-thirds of primary schools now operate without trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2020, the Ministry piloted the removal of CCA selection trials across eight primary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, about two-thirds of primary schools operate without trials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: When I asked the Minister about this on 12 February, the reply confirmed the results but did not address secondary schools where LEAPS 2.0 applies and stakes are highest.

sections.label: DSA secondary school coverage
sections.summary: DSA now covers 141 of 148 secondary schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: DSA now covers 141 of 148 secondary schools.

sections.label: Basketball coach DSA investigation
sections.summary: In 2024, a basketball coach was investigated by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau for allegedly charging parents $30,000 to $50,000 per child for DSA placements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In 2024, a basketball coach was investigated by the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau for allegedly charging parents $30,000 to $50,000 per child to secure DSA placements.

sections.label: Science study on top performers
sections.summary: A December 2025 study in Science synthesising over 34,000 top-level performers found young standouts and adult world-class performers are largely different people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In December 2025, a study was published in major journal Science, synthesising the developmental histories of over 34,000 top-level performers – Olympic athletes, Nobel laureates, elite chess players, classical music composers – and had a central finding: young standouts and adult world-class performers are largely different people.

sections.label: Measuring programme success by transitions
sections.summary: The passage states programme success should be measured by athletes transitioning to senior international excellence, and that the CCA system is structurally an early-selection model.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Also, that programme success should be measured not by junior medals, but by how many athletes transition to senior international excellence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This matters because our CCA system – trials at age 12, a four-year lock-in, LEAPS points tied to competitive results – is structurally an early-selection model.

sections.label: SP-CCA programme expansion plan
sections.summary: The SP-CCA programme serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports, and one plan is to double it to eight sports within two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Strategic Partnership CCA (SP-CCA) programme today serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, to double SP-CCA from four sports to eight sports within two years.

sections.label: CCA recognition and Junior Sports Academy
sections.summary: Asks whether students in external programmes could get CCA recognition, and whether Junior Sports Academy intake could be doubled or tripled.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Could students participating in a structured external programme – ActiveSG, a National Sports Association, or a registered academy – be eligible for CCA recognition, subject to verification by the school?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And at primary level, could we double or triple the Junior Sports Academy intake – this fully Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded, non-competitive, multi-sport programme – given demand already exceeds supply?

sections.label: Coach certification requirements since July 2024
sections.summary: Since July 2024 provisional membership ended, and new coaches must complete SG-Coach Theory, a Technical Level 1 course, Foundational Sport Science and First Aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since July 2024, provisional membership has been discontinued.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A new coach must now complete SG-Coach Theory, a sport-specific Technical Level 1 course, Foundational Sport Science and Standard First Aid certification.

sections.label: Proposed new NROC assistant coach tier
sections.summary: Proposes CoachSG create an Assistant or Recreational Coach NROC tier of eight to 16 hours, whose holders lead developmental CCA sessions under supervision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: CoachSG's own framework already includes an Exploration stage with a Community Coach programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I propose that CoachSG create a new NROC tier – an Assistant Coach or Recreational Coach credential, completable in eight to 16 hours at nominal cost, covering maybe Safe Sport, first-aid, values-based coaching and inclusive session design.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Holders could lead developmental CCA sessions under periodic supervision by fully certified coaches.

sections.label: LEAPS measures and DSA socio-economic data
sections.summary: Proposes replacing competition-based indicators with growth, effort and consistency measures, and requiring MOE to publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Replacing competition-based indicators with measures of growth, effort and consistency would realign LEAPS to its developmental purpose.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And require MOE to collect and publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes – household income quartile, participation in paid preparatory programmes.

sections.label: 1966 extra-curricular activities purpose
sections.summary: In 1966, Minister for Education Ong Pang Boon identified extra-curricular activities as a means to inculcate moral values and national identity and pride.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: In 1966, during our early years of nation-building, then-Minister for Education Mr Ong Pang Boon identified extra-curricular activities (ECAs) as a means to inculcate moral values and a sense of national identity and pride among our youths.

sections.label: Renaming ECAs as CCAs in 1999
sections.summary: In 1999, ECAs were renamed CCAs, increasing their importance to reflect these aspirations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: In 1999, we reflected these aspirations and we increased its importance by renaming ECAs as CCAs.

sections.label: CCA grading scheme LEAPS
sections.summary: A CCA grading scheme, LEAPS, was introduced in 2003, and LEAPS 2.0 followed in 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: To encourage students' continued participation in a broad and diverse range of non-academic activities, a CCA grading scheme, LEAPS, which the Member mentioned was introduced in 2003.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: The introduction of LEAPS 2.0 in 2014 also marked another step forward.

sections.label: MOE and MCCY sharing facilities
sections.summary: MOE and MCCY, including Sport Singapore and the National Arts Council, work together to share facilities and provide coaching across schools.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: MOE and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), in particular Sport Singapore and the National Arts Council, are working together to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools.

sections.label: MOE Opportunity Fund for students
sections.summary: Minister Desmond Lee said students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for learning experiences and CCA expenses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Minister Desmond Lee, in his COS speech this morning, has said that students from lower-income families can tap on the MOE Opportunity Fund for learning experiences and any additional CCA expenses.

sections.label: Junior Sports Academy access
sections.summary: The Junior Sports Academy programme lets primary school students discover sporting strengths and interests, and access to it will be explored.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Of note also, is the Junior Sports Academy programmme for primary school students to discover their sporting strengths and interests, something that the Member has also spoken about.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: And yes, we will explore how to increase access to the Junior Sports Academy programme as well.

sections.label: Strengthening CCA access priority
sections.summary: MOE and MCCY will work to strengthen CCAs' role in holistic development, with access a key priority, including first choice and disadvantaged students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, we will work across ministries, both MOE and MCCY, to continue to strengthen the role that CCAs play in nurturing the holistic development of our students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: And as part of this, strengthening access to CCAs for students is a key priority, including allowing more of them their first choice and strengthening access for students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

sections.label: MOE commitment to CCA access
sections.summary: MOE remains committed to working with teachers, parents and partners so students can access CCAs that nurture heart and mind.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
sentences.text: MOE remains committed to working closely with teachers, parents and partners across Government and the community to ensure that students continue to be able to access CCAs and that CCAs continue to nurture both the heart and mind so that we continue to shape a generation that is not just ready for work, but for life.
